 Dated this the 15th day of March, 2024
 Order
This is a petition filed by the appellant under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
(Code).
The petitioner would contend that he is innocent and there is every chance for allowing t
he appeal and acquitting him
. He was on bail during the trial of the case.
In such circumstances, he claims that he is entitled to get execution of his sentence suspended.
2. The learned Public Prosecutor filed an objection on behalf of the respondent.
It is contended that the evidence adduced by the prosecution proved beyond doubt that the petitioner had committed the offence alleged against him.
The offence proved against the petitioner is grievous.
(On account of the offence he has committed and the consequent ostracisation, the victim, who was aged only 8 years at the time of occurrence, has been put to untold miseries.
Considering the gravity and nature of the offence and the in tenure of the sentence imposed the petitioner is not entitled to get an order to suspend the sentence.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. Petitioner was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The term of Sentence the petitioner has to undergo is imprisonment for 10 years.

5. The charge levelled against the petitioner was that the petitioner who is the father of the victim repeatedly assaulted her sexually from the year 2012 onwards and he committed carnal intercourse on the victim several occasions from 2015 onwards.
The trial court believing the evidence tendered by the prosecution found the petitioner guilty as mentioned above.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there have been serious discrepancies in the evidence of the victim .
Therefore, the conviction is based on unreliable in and insufficient evidence, and the appeal will be allowed.
Having gone through the judgment and considered the available materials, prima facie, I am unable to agree with the contention that the findings leading to conviction of the petitioner are wrong.

7. The learned Public Prosecutor would submit that considering the serious nature of the offence,
the petitioner has committed, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
Especially when he is the father of the victim.
8. The period of sentence imposed is 10 years.
He was convicted and sentenced on 25.09.2020 and has been in jail since then.
The contentions raised by the petitioner to assail the impugned judgment require deeper consideration.
The petitioner has been in jail for about four years.
The likelihood of hearing and disposing the appeal immediately is remote, owing to the pendency of older appeals.
Considering that and other mitigating circumstances, I am of the view that execution of sentence can be suspended subject to conditions.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to apply before this Court for cancellation of the suspension of sentence.
